removed: - owns: `/etc/w2c/configstore-rights.json` (the form — N1.2; written by the rights derivation of [P/02.5](../../02-installer/spec/02.5-installer.norms.md) N3 «generate_rights»);
- writes: no rows;
- reads: no rows — the evaluator answers about any rows by the patterns of the rights file.
`console` writes the operator rows of all manifests.
`domain` is the signer with keys, `domainconsole` has no keys (P/08.2 N1.3).
`configstore` is the role of a peer, another daemon of the group.
`configstore-door` is the door without a vote (added by P/01.3 N1.3).
`domainworker` maps to the role `<sub>domain` of a manifest that has `domain.kept` or a portable book (P/03.7 N1.6: a platform capability, not the removed process `domainpart`).
`domainworker` does not enter the comparison «declared = able to read».
`<sub>` of a role name follows the grammar of the manifest name (P/02.1).
The deployment name matches `deployment`.
The group of `<role>.sock` is `SocketGroup=` of the socket unit (P/02.4 N1.1).
On a box the identity is the writer's name at a store of files/memory.
On a box the writer's name has the same list of rights.
The box door also opens a socket per role.
The optional field `comment` of the file is a string.
`comment` is the generator's mark; it takes no part in granting rights.
The mark necessarily names that the file is generated, the deployment, the source manifests and «do not edit by hand».
For the same inputs the text of the mark is the same (P/02.5-01).
Each role has the required `group` (a non-empty string), `read` and `write` (arrays of strings).
`delete` of a role is an optional array of strings.
Unknown fields are rejected.
Role names are checked whole, including the end of the string.
The internal roles of the store are not in the file: the file does not name `admin`, `configstore`, `configstore-door`.
The generator always writes `delete` for every role: it equals `write`, unless the manifest separated them by `delete:`.
A `*` as the last character makes the pattern a prefix (`prefix`).
A `*` not last is a literal character.
A `!` only as the first character makes the pattern a negation (`deny`).
A negation wins everywhere in the list.
The patterns of `literal` are admissible in the file.

The patterns of `literal` match by the rules above: `""` — only the empty key, `"!"` — the negation of the empty key, `"!*"` — the negation of everything (vector Platform/01-store/vectors/rights-evaluator).
A `!` not first is a literal character (a `*` not last — P/01.2-R115).
The file is not edited by hand.
There is no live reload of the file.
Without the file only `admin.sock` opens.
The name of a derived role is not truncated.
never holds for admin too.

The epoch row of never is `<x>/epoch/<y>`: `x` is exactly one nonempty key segment other than `platform` and contains no slash; `y` is exactly one segment and may be empty (P/01.2-R122, P/01.2-R123). This is the same grammar used by upper (P/01.3-R408).
In the epoch row of never x ≠ platform.
A domain role is the name `domain`, `domainagent` or `<sub>domain` (`<sub>` — the grammar of the subsystem name of P/02.1, `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`).
never checks under `domain/` only the domain role.

«Their own families» of the domain roles are set by the delete patterns of the rights file derived by the generator (P/02.5, the `--check` comparison); the store does not re-check them against the catalogue.
A listing gives no values.
A guard does not extend rights.
A batch (P/01.1 N3 «write batch») is judged per row: write or delete of every row of writes.
In a batch never is judged per row, for admin too.
A refusal of one row of a batch is a refusal of the whole batch.
Request parsing at the rights doors is chapter 1.1 N2.1.
For `GET /v1/rights` the query is not read.
The HTTP contract: [01-store.api.openapi.yaml](01-store.api.openapi.yaml).
While no file is loaded, the route `/v1/rights` answers `404 badrequest`; an empty object `roles` does not stand in for the absence of the file.

The `404` of `/v1/rights` without a file MUST come after the identity: the row `rc-rights_absent` of [`rights-checks.tsv`](../forms/rights-checks.tsv) stands after `rc-rights_not_admin`, so an identity that is not admin gets `403` and only admin learns that the file is absent.
Access to `/v1/rights` is checked by the identity admin, before the file is given out: the row `rc-rights_not_admin` of [`rights-checks.tsv`](../forms/rights-checks.tsv).
A successful `GET /v1/list` uses the `Listing` of chapter 1.1: without the values of rows, with versions and the order of names by UTF-8 bytes.
The presence of the path is checked for list too.
The absence of the read right does not prevent listing.
The `kind` of the refusals `400`, `403`, `404`, `503` of the two routes is respectively `badrequest`, `forbidden`, `badrequest`, `unavailable`.
For a refusal of the identity itself or of `/v1/rights`, `error` names the role and the cause/route.
With a role header on a role socket, `error` names the role of the socket, not the role imposed by the header; parsing the key of the operation for diagnostics is not required.
A role header on a role socket is the row `rc-role_header`:\nafter the frame (chapter 1.1 R217), before the body is parsed (a body out of form with such a header is also `403`).
If the role is forwarded, the ban on a forwarded admin (P/01.2-R090) is checked before the other rows of the rights.

Steps 4–6 together are the function `allowed` of the tables; the read of `/v1/get` is the row `rc-read_forbidden`;\na write and a delete are the rows `wc-rights` and `wc-write_rights` of [`write-checks.tsv`](../forms/write-checks.tsv).
If one right of a batch is refused, return `403` for the whole batch, before the record to the log.
The absence of the file does not turn off the check of trust in the sender.
- `list_form`: `/v1/list` out of the form of chapter 1.1 N2.1 (a repeated `prefix`). Caller action: fix the request.
- `rights_no_route`, `rights_store_unavailable`: no route; the store is unavailable (`/v1/list`, `/v1/rights`). Caller action: —.
- `read_forbidden`: a read without the right. Caller action: a deployment error or a foreign process.
- `write_forbidden`: a write/delete without the right. Caller action: the same.
- `guard_read_forbidden`: a guard on a row without the read right. Caller action: the same.
- `never`: a delete of an epoch row; a delete under `domain/` by a role that is not a domain role; a write and a delete of `platform/epoch_floor`. Caller action: never.
- `role_header`: a role header on a role socket. Caller action: a client error.
- `forwarding_untrusted`: a forwarding not from a daemon of the group (a voting one or the door without a vote); a forwarded `admin` with a loaded rights file. Caller action: —.
- `rights_not_admin`: `/v1/rights`: the identity is not admin after the check of admissibility of the forwarding. Caller action: —.
- `rights_not_loaded`: `/v1/rights`: the file is not loaded. Caller action: set up the file and restart.
- `rights_file_form`: the rights file is out of form; it names `admin`/`configstore`/`configstore-door`; a role not by the grammar. Caller action: regenerate.
